articles.headline: Contract Year Focus Shapes Paddock Dynamics
articles.dek: Several veterans enter the 2026 season operating on expiring deals as silly season conversations quietly begin.
articles.body:
As the garage area unpacks for the season opener at Daytona International Speedway, attention extends beyond immediate on-track performance and into the business office. Several prominent drivers and part-time competitors enter the 2026 schedule with contracts expiring at the conclusion of the year, setting the stage for potential movement across multiple series.

Stewart Friesen enters the season in the final year of his agreement with Halmar Friesen Racing. Sources close to the team indicate that stability remains the priority for the veteran driver, who enters the year content with his current equipment package. Similarly, veteran Timmy Hill operates on an expiring deal with Hill Motorsports while balancing part-time entries and organizational growth.

Makeshift evaluations also apply to part-time competitors looking toward future opportunities in higher divisions. Drivers such as Connor Zilisch, Christopher Bell, and Ross Chastain carry expiring agreements while managing dual-series expectations. Industry chatter suggests that strong performances in the Craftsman Truck Series could influence potential promotions into the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series, where seats at organizations like Richard Childress Racing or JR Motorsports could see turnover.

Team executives have maintained a quiet posture regarding future commitments while focusing entirely on the twenty-five-race schedule ahead. With the season yet to officially commence, formal negotiations remain limited to sponsor renewals and minor paint scheme finalizations for the current campaign. No definitive driver announcements for subsequent seasons are expected until the summer months provide a clearer competitive baseline.

For now, the primary objective across the pit lane involves maximizing every available stage point and race win. Expiring contracts provide an underlying narrative for veterans and rising talents alike, but the immediate pressure rests entirely on securing a strong finish in the season opener.
articles.author: Cole Whitaker

Silly season discussions remain quiet as the racing season begins.

articles.headline: Zilisch Leads Daytona Preseason Test Speed Charts
articles.dek: Spire Motorsports driver sets the pace in the final tune-up before the Fresh From Florida 250.
articles.body:
Spire Motorsports driver Connor Zilisch paced the field during the preseason testing session at Daytona International Speedway, laying down a lap of 49.821 seconds in the #77 machine to lead the speed charts. Teams utilized the track time to evaluate drafting tandems and run various aerodynamic setups ahead of the official season opener.

Stewart Friesen followed closely in the second position driving the #52 Halmar Friesen Racing entry. Friesen, operating in the final year of his current contract, focused heavily on race trim during the drafting simulations. Kaden Honeycutt rounded out the top three for Tricon Garage, clocking the third-fastest time in the #11 truck.

ThorSport Racing placed Cole Butcher fourth overall, while Frankie Muniz rounded out the top five in the #33 Team Reaume entry. Other notable participants in the top twenty included Tanner Gray in sixth, Adam Andretti in seventh, and Timmy Hill in eighth. Drivers utilized the multi-lane racing surface to test different lines through the high-banked turns, though several teams elected to remain in the garage during the peak heat of the afternoon.

The test session serves as the final on-track activity before technical inspection opens for the Fresh From Florida 250. Crew chiefs will review telemetry data overnight to determine gear ratios and cooling configurations for the opening race of the 2026 calendar.

Track officials reported no major incidents during the two-day test, allowing every entered organization to complete its checklist without structural damage. Qualifying for the season opener is scheduled for Friday morning, followed by the 250-mile race later that evening.
articles.author: Jamie Kowalski

articles.headline: Tiering the Field for the 2026 Craftsman Truck Series Season
articles.dek: A comprehensive breakdown of title favorites, emerging contenders, and garage tiers as the field prepares to open the year at Daytona.
articles.body:
As the virtual Craftsman Truck Series prepares to open its 2026 campaign, the paddock settles into familiar hierarchies while new technical alliances take shape. With twenty-five races on the docket before the championship battle crystallizes, the preseason test at Daytona International Speedway provided the first tangible data points for analysts tracking winter development programs.

At the top of the board, established operations like ThorSport Racing and Tricon Garage look to dictate the pace. ThorSport brings a deep stable featuring Cole Butcher, Jake Garcia, Ben Rhodes, and Ty Majeski. Butcher flashed early speed during testing by clocking the fourth-fastest lap in the #13 machine, signaling that ThorSport's superspeedway package remains sharp. Tricon counters with a heavy-hitting lineup including Kaden Honeycutt, Tanner Gray, Adam Andretti, Nick Leitz, and Gio Ruggiero. Honeycutt established his baseline quickly at Daytona with the third-quickest time overall, positioning himself as a primary threat in the early rounds.

Moving into the dark horse category, equipment from McAnally-Hilgemann Racing and Niece Motorsports could disrupt the traditional powerhouse teams. McAnally fields Daniel Dye, Daniel Hemric, Tyler Ankrum, Christian Eckes, and Kris Wright. Their focus during the Daytona test centered on drafting lines and single-lap trim rather than pure headline speeds. Niece brings Ross Chastain, Andrés Pérez de Lara, Cleetus McFarland, and Parker Eatmon to the track. Chastain enters the year under a contract-year designation, adding organizational motivation to his part-time schedule in the #42 entry.

Spire Motorsports demands attention with a high-profile roster that features Connor Zilisch, Kyle Busch, Shane Van Gisbergen, and Connor Mosack. Zilisch dominated the timesheets in testing by topping the speed chart with the quickest lap in the #77 truck. While Daytona speeds often reflect drafting help rather than raw horsepower, pacing the test session gives Spire an immediate psychological advantage. As the circuit shifts from the drafting drills of Daytona toward intermediate tracks, these early tier divisions will face their first real competitive pressure.
articles.author: Wes Ostrander
